theme: Jehoram, Athaliah, Joash, the throne preserved
readingInstruction: Read 2 Chronicles 21:1-24:27. Jehoram and Ahaziah lead Judah into evil, Athaliah usurps the throne, and young Joash is rescued and crowned. Joash starts well under the priest Jehoiada and then falls. Watch how the Chronicler explains the change.
settingTheScene: Jehoshaphat’s alliance with Ahab leads to the marriage of his son Jehoram to Athaliah, Ahab’s daughter. The consequence is tragic. Jehoram kills his brothers, Ahaziah is killed, and Athaliah slaughters the royal family except for one baby, Joash. The line of David hangs by a thread. This is the low point of Judah’s early history.
observation: “And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab was his wife” (21:6).
“Yet the LORD was not willing to destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that he had made with David” (21:7).
“Jehosheba… took Joash the son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king’s sons who were being put to death” (22:11).
“Behold, the king’s son! Let him reign, as the LORD spoke concerning the sons of David” (23:3).
“And Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest” (24:2).
“But after the death of Jehoiada the officials of Judah came and paid homage to the king” (24:17).
“The Spirit of God clothed Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, and he stood above the people” (24:20).
“Thus Joash the king did not remember the kindness that Jehoiada, Zechariah’s father, had shown him, but killed his son” (24:22).
interpretation:
Chapter 21 shows how a bad alliance bears bitter fruit. Jehoram marries Ahab’s daughter and imports Baal worship. He murders his six brothers, and God sends an Edomite revolt and a Philistine and Arab raid. Elijah sends a letter of judgment. He dies in agony of the bowels, and “no one desired his departure.” It is a terrible epitaph.

Yet the Chronicler adds a note of mercy: “The LORD was not willing to destroy the house of David, because of the covenant.” God’s faithfulness to his promise is bigger than the faithlessness of the kings. And at the lowest moment, when Athaliah murders the heirs of David, God has a baby hidden. Jehosheba, the king’s daughter and wife of the priest Jehoiada, saves Joash and hides him in the temple for six years. The promise to David depended on a woman’s courage.

Jehoiada then stages the coup. He gathers the Levites and the commanders, brings out the boy king, and crowns him. The priest makes a covenant between God, the king, and the people. The people rejoice, and the city is quiet. Athaliah is put to death, and the Baal altar is torn down.

Joash starts well, repairing the temple with a collection from the people. But Jehoiada dies at 130, and everything changes. The officials come and persuade the king, and “they abandoned the house of the LORD… and served the Asherim and the idols.” Joash’s faith had been a borrowed faith, propped up by his mentor. When God sends prophets, the king responds by having Zechariah, the priest’s son, stoned in the temple court. “May the LORD see and avenge.”

The tragedy of Joash is that he never made the faith his own. The lesson is to build a faith that stands even when the people who first taught you are gone.
connection: 2 Timothy 1:5 praises the faith that dwelt in Timothy’s grandmother and mother, and now in him. Matthew 23:35 refers to the blood of Zechariah, who was killed between the temple and the altar. Hebrews 3:12: “Take care, brothers, lest there be in any of you an evil, unbelieving heart.” 2 Corinthians 6:14: do not be unequally yoked. Jude 24: “Now to him who is able to keep you from stumbling.”
application:
Ask whether your faith depends on a person or a community more than on your own walk with God. Take a step to own it.

Thank someone who played the role of Jehoiada in your life.

Be a Jehoiada to a young person: protect, teach, and pray.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for his faithfulness when his people fail.
Thank him for preserving David’s line.
Ask him to keep you from taking his patience for granted.
